s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic abdominal symptoms with weight loss and bowel obstruction
salient_findings: Worsening abdominal distention and 60-lb unintentional weight loss over 1 year
Small-bowel obstruction with focal wall thickening and mesenteric adenopathy
Multiple small-bowel ulcers and atrophic duodenum
Jejunal strictures and areas suggestive of inflammatory bowel disease
Perforated ulcer in the terminal ileum
key_facts: 55-year-old man with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and opioid use disorder
Presented with worsening abdominal distention and unintentional weight loss
Increasing difficulty with bowel movements
Denied melena, nausea, vomiting, fevers, flank pain, dysphagia, or odynophagia
Abdominal CT showed small-bowel obstruction with transition point in right-mid abdomen
Colonoscopy revealed two polyps with non-specific chronic inflammation
Video capsule endoscopy demonstrated erythematous gastritis and multiple small-bowel ulcers
Double-balloon enteroscopy identified multiple jejunal strictures
Exploratory laparotomy revealed perforated ulcer in terminal ileum
Biopsies around perforation showed ulcerated mucosa with non-specific chronic inflammation
Ileoscopy showed scalloped mucosa with blunted villi throughout ileum
Histologic examination revealed extensive lymphocytic infiltrates with epitheliotropism

shortlist.label: Crohn's disease
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic abdominal symptoms, weight loss, bowel obstruction, and small-bowel ulcers

shortlist.label: Intestinal lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Perforated ulcer, lymphocytic infiltrates, and epitheliotropism on histologic examination

shortlist.label: Ulcerative colitis
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic abdominal symptoms, weight loss, and non-specific chronic inflammation on colonoscopy

shortlist.label: NSAID-induced enteropathy
shortlist.why_kept: History of chronic abdominal symptoms and small-bowel ulcers

shortlist.label: Eosinophilic gastroenteritis
shortlist.why_kept: Erythematous gastritis and small-bowel ulcers on video capsule endoscopy

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with worsening abdominal distention, unintentional weight loss, and increasing difficulty with bowel movements, along with findings of small-bowel obstruction, multiple jejunal strictures, and perforated ulcer in the terminal ileum, are consistent with Crohn's disease. The histologic examination revealing extensive lymphocytic infiltrates with epitheliotropism also supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Intestinal lymphoma
rejected.why: While the histologic examination showed lymphocytic infiltrates, there were no definitive atypical morphological features to support a diagnosis of lymphoma.

rejected.label: Ulcerative colitis
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and findings are more consistent with small-bowel involvement, which is less typical of ulcerative colitis.

rejected.label: NSAID-induced enteropathy
rejected.why: There is no mention of NSAID use in the patient's history, making this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Eosinophilic gastroenteritis
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and findings do not specifically suggest eosinophilic gastroenteritis, and the histologic examination did not reveal eosinophilic infiltration.
